title: ABT: Long, hold 16 sh and size the add on tonight's re-mark. Q3 cut the growth guide but kept EPS; research target (12m) $107.79 at 17x, target $110.95
call_reason: The published target ($110.95) and the research target (12m) of $107.79 are above the $102.45 pre-print close, with P(gain) 0.6116 and sizing confidence medium. The edge is modest: the supervisor's confidence is low and it claims no directional edge.
one_liner: Q3 held the earnings line: adj. EPS $1.42 and the FY2026 $5.50-5.55 midpoint reaffirmed. It cut the growth line: comparable growth ~6.0%, diabetes low-to-mid single digit, and a Nutrition spin by end-2027. At 17.0x a below-consensus ~$6.43 NTM EPS, net of ~$2.7B of litigation and separation cash, ABT is worth $107.79 (+9.6% vs the $98.36 post-print quote, derived: 107.79 / 98.36 - 1), so we keep the 16 sh @ $102.80 and stage the second tranche, which tonight's post-print re-mark sizes (+18 sh on the pre-print plan).

thesis.point: The print cut growth, not earnings, and our EPS already sits below the street.
thesis.evidence: Q3 adj. EPS $1.42 (+9.2%) on $13,013M sales (+7.0% comparable). The FY2026 adj. EPS midpoint was reaffirmed and the range narrowed to $5.50-5.55, and Q4 is guided to $1.62-1.67. The comparable-growth guide fell to ~6.0% (prior memo: 6.5-7.5%). Our horizon NTM adj. EPS of ~$6.43 (supervisor build) comes from that guide: FY2027 ~$6.06 and FY2028 ~$6.52, 0.3% and 3.2% under the pre-print Zacks consensus of $6.08 / $6.74 (supervisor figures on unrounded EPS; derived on the rounded figures: 6.06 / 6.08 - 1 = -0.3%, 6.52 / 6.74 - 1 = -3.3%), and 2.7% under a horizon-NTM consensus of ~$6.61 (derived: ~0.2 x $6.08 + ~0.8 x $6.74 = $6.61; 6.43 / 6.61 - 1 = -2.7%). Street cuts after the guide change should mostly converge toward our numbers, not below them.

thesis.point: The valuation needs no re-rating. We price 17.0x, which keeps a ~7% discount to peers and is only ~3% above today's multiple (derived: 17.0 / 18.2 - 1 = -6.6%; 17.0 / 16.5 - 1 = +3.0%).
thesis.evidence: On one calendar NTM window (2026-10-21 to 2027-10-20), ABT trades at 16.5x against an 18.2x median for 11 peers (supervisor rebase, derived: ABT $98.36 / (0.197 x $5.53 + 0.803 x $6.08 = $5.97) = 16.5x). The P/E leg uses 17.0x and the EV/EBITDA leg 13.3x, which is ABT's own multiple today (derived: EV ~$198.6B / ~$14.88B NTM adj. EBITDA in the build = 13.35x). The discount persists through the horizon for three reasons: Nutrition plus EPD are ~22% of FY2027 segment operating earnings in the reconciled build (derived: (1,621 + 1,481) / 14,277 = 21.7%; FY2025 10-K actual (1,558 + 1,290) / 11,800 = 24.1%) at staples/generics multiples until a spin that most likely lands after 2027-10-20, CGM growth is slower and Medicare bidding pricing starts ~2028, and ~12,700 NEC infants are still pending. The 17.0x / 13.3x multiple was chosen on the 2026-10-21 decision card over the 18.2x / 14.0x peer median, which would give $115.00 (supervisor).

thesis.point: The known liabilities are now sized and deducted. The Nutrition separation is value-neutral, and any re-rating it brings is upside we do not count.
thesis.evidence: The research target (12m) deducts ~$2.67B after tax (derived: 520 + 350 + 750 + 150 + 600 + 300 = $2,670M): the ~$670M NEC deal (-$520M), the $384.2M DOJ/states settlement (-$350M), the ~12,700 remaining NEC infants (-$750M, supervisor estimate; derived: ~$970M pre-tax / ~12,700 = ~$76k per infant, ~2x the August deal's ~$35k = (~$670M - ~$600M Gill) / ~2,000), Libre 3 recall claims (-$300M x 0.5), specified-items cash (-$600M) and separation costs (-$300M). The 8-K describes a distribution of a ~$8.5B-sales Nutrition company, intended to qualify as tax-free, completion expected by end-2027, with a combined dividend equal to Abbott's. We carry a 10% chance that it distributes before 2027-10-20, which moves only the quote (~$9 lower on a distribution of equal value; derived by the supervisor as the mean of two agent estimates, ($10.7 + $7.35) / 2 = ~$9.0).

variant_view: The variant view is small, and it points the other way from the street. Our $110.95 target and $107.79 research target (12m) sit well below the sell-side: mean $120.72, median $120, 28 analysts, Strong Buy, as of 2026-10-16 before the print, given zero weight. We think the street is stale. Pre-print FY2027/FY2028 consensus of $6.08 / $6.74 predates the cut to ~6.0% comparable growth, diabetes at low-to-mid single digit 'for the next few quarters', and EP guided to ~20% in Q4, and our build is already 0.3% / 3.2% below it. Against the options market we are only slightly more constructive: the market-only distribution has a $107.35 median and P(gain) 0.5633, against the published $110.95 and 0.6116. The research leg alone gives $110.78 / 0.6191. The supervisor's reconciled value ($107.79) sits on the five forecasters' mean ($107.67), and the supervisor claims no directional edge. Read this as a fairly priced, defensive compounder bought slightly below value, not a mispricing the market is missing. (Sources 1, 3, 9, 23, 24, 25.)

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) is $107.79, the model engine's base horizon value (2027-10-20) on the supervisor's reconciled inputs. It weights 0.6 x P/E (17.0x NTM adj. EPS of ~$6.43) and 0.4 x EV/EBITDA (13.3x NTM adj. EBITDA); both legs come to $107.79. It is net of ~$2.67B after-tax litigation, settlement, separation and specified-items cash, on 2026-06-30 net debt of $27,005M (derived: 3,005 + 29,603 - 5,104 - 499, 10-Q). Scenarios: bear $78.79 / base $107.79 / bull $132.55. The five agents' research targets (12m) run $104.53-$110.82 (median $107.96; mean $107.67, derived: (110.82 + 108.80 + 104.53 + 107.96 + 106.26) / 5). The multiple decision card gave three values: 17.0x / 13.3x at $107.79 (chosen), the 18.2x / 14.0x peer median at $115.00 ($114.92 before the citation-gate fixes), and today's 16.5x / 13.0x at $104.75. There is no DCF leg this round; the prior memo blended 0.4 DCF. The $110.95 target is the median of the published 12-month distribution, which weights the options market 0.67 and research 0.33 with a calibration shift (expected value $115.03). It is not the research target (12m). Upside from the $102.45 pre-print close is +8.30% to target and +5.21% to the research target (12m) (derived: 110.95 / 102.45 - 1; 107.79 / 102.45 - 1). From the $98.36 post-print quote it is +12.8% and +9.6% (derived: 110.95 / 98.36 - 1; 107.79 / 98.36 - 1). Changes vs the 2026-10-14 memo: target $110.01 to $110.95 (+$0.94), research target (12m) $114.08 to $107.79 (derived: -$6.29, -5.5%), TP $130.57 to $133.60, stop $82.51 to $82.70, thesis break $80 to $78. The research target (12m) fell on 17.5x to 17.0x, dropping the DCF leg, slower Libre and EP after the call, and a fuller litigation/separation deduction. All levels are from the pre-print 2026-10-20 close and are re-marked tonight on the post-print close. (Sources 6, 7, 11, 24, 25, 30, 31, 36.)

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and the Nutrition separation announcement (already out; the levels in this memo predate the reaction)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The comparable-growth guide fell to ~6.0% and diabetes was guided to low-to-mid single digit for several quarters. EPS was in line ($1.42) with the FY midpoint held, and the 8-K announced the Nutrition spin by end-2027.
catalysts.watch: The post-print close that the nightly re-mark uses. ABT traded at $98.36 intraday (low $97.73) vs the $102.45 close. The supervisor's 1-month ladder from ~$98.4 gives P(>= $102.45) = 0.291.

catalysts.event: Boston Scientific Q3 2026 results (electrophysiology / PFA read-across)
catalysts.why_it_moves: EP is ABT's fastest device line (+15.5% comparable in Q3), and management just cut Q4 EP growth to ~20%. BSX Farapulse share and pricing frame how much of that is ABT-specific.
catalysts.watch: BSX EP growth, PFA pricing, and any LAA demand comment (ABT blamed LAA orders for the EP cut).

catalysts.event: Dexcom Q3 2026 results, after the close (CGM read-across)
catalysts.why_it_moves: CGM is ABT's key debate after the diabetes guide-down. Dexcom's US pricing, type 2 penetration and CMS coverage commentary test whether the slowdown is category-wide or Libre share loss.
catalysts.watch: US CGM growth and pricing, any update on Medicare non-insulin type 2 coverage, and the 2027 commentary.

catalysts.event: TCT 2026: one-year Amulet 360 LAA outcomes in the late-breaking program; on the call an analyst named the Amulet 360 and coronary IVL pivotal readouts and the CEO confirmed 'two important readouts for us at TCT'
catalysts.why_it_moves: LAA order softness after the new Amulet's CE Mark drove the Q4 EP cut. Clean data could support the claim that Q4 is the last quarter of the headwind.
catalysts.watch: Amulet 360 leak and complication rates vs Watchman, and the IVL pivotal endpoints and approval timing (first half per management).

catalysts.why_it_moves: It gives the first net debt after the NEC and DOJ payments (the model still uses 2026-06-30), plus the NEC docket count and any separation or Libre litigation disclosure.
catalysts.watch: Net debt vs the ~$27.0B at 6/30, the NEC suit and infant counts vs ~1,700 / ~12,700, and any new accruals.

catalysts.event: Medtronic FQ2 FY2027 results (last year's FQ2 came on 2025-11-18)
catalysts.why_it_moves: It is a read on diabetes (Medtronic still reports Diabetes; its MiniMed 780G pairs with the Instinct sensor made by Abbott) and on cardiac ablation share against Volt / TactiFlex Duo.
catalysts.watch: MiniMed CGM attach and Cardiac Ablation Solutions growth.

catalysts.event: Full US launch of the TactiFlex Duo ablation catheter and the Volt PFA launch in Japan (company-stated quarter)
catalysts.why_it_moves: These launches drive the 2027 EP re-acceleration that management expects.
catalysts.watch: Launch confirmation and early share commentary at the January call.

catalysts.event: US launch of Libre Duo, the glucose-ketone sensor (FDA-approved August 2026; the CEO stated December on the call)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Management named it a 2027 diabetes growth driver. A slip would add to the CGM concern.
catalysts.watch: Launch on time, payer coverage, and early uptake in type 1 / insulin users.

catalysts.why_it_moves: It signals board confidence after the guide cut. The CEO pointed to continued dividend growth.

catalysts.event: US payer formulary coverage change that 'flipped in our favor', effective January 1 (CEO, Q3 call, in his diabetes remarks; the product is not named in that sentence)
catalysts.why_it_moves: It is the main stated lever for US Libre growth to beat the low-to-mid single-digit guide in 2027.
catalysts.watch: Q1 2027 US Libre growth and any quantification on the January call.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results and first FY2027 guidance (Abbott states 2027 guidance comes in January)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This sets the EPS base for the horizon valuation (~$6.43 NTM). Last January's initial FY2026 guide ($5.55-5.80) was lowered to $5.38-5.58 in April, incl. ~$0.20 Exact dilution, and the street ($6.08 pre-print) is likely to drift down.
catalysts.watch: FY2027 adj. EPS vs ~$6.0 (our FY2027 ~$6.06; a guide well below $6.0 points toward the $78 thesis break), organic growth vs ~6%, the diabetes and EP outlook, and the first separation cost figures.

catalysts.date: 2026-Q4 to 2027 (no date; CEO would not forecast)
catalysts.event: CMS decision on Medicare CGM coverage for non-insulin type 2 patients
catalysts.why_it_moves: The CEO said it is not in the near-term forecast. The supervisor carries it only as upside (~30% probability, ~+$1.3/share).
catalysts.watch: A proposed or final LCD, its effective date and eligibility criteria.

catalysts.event: Form 10 filing for the new Nutrition company (no name announced): capital structure, debt raised and cash paid to Abbott, stranded costs, one-time charges
catalysts.why_it_moves: The terms decide whether the spin is truly value-neutral. Large stranded costs or a small cash payment would hurt RemainCo, while clean terms could start a RemainCo re-rating.
catalysts.watch: The new company's debt and the payment to Abbott, stranded costs vs the ~$300M after-tax separation cash we deduct, and timing vs end-2027.

catalysts.event: Q1 2027 results: the first quarter with the formulary change in effect; Exact Sciences (acquired 2026-03-23) is in the prior-year quarter for only its last ~8 days, so reported Cancer Dx growth stays inflated until Q2 2027
catalysts.why_it_moves: It is the first test of the FY2027 guide and of the diabetes trough. Last April's print came with a guide cut.
catalysts.watch: Diabetes growth vs low-to-mid single digit, EP vs ~20%, and whether the FY2027 guide is held.

catalysts.event: Section 232 medical-device tariff decision (the Federal Register lists no presidential Section 232 proclamation on medical devices as of 2026-10-21)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Commerce's notice (initiated 2025-09-02) lists blood glucose monitors, pacemakers, insulin pumps and coronary stents among example devices. The supervisor holds it in the bear case only (30%, ~-$0.6/share).
catalysts.watch: A proclamation, its scope (CGM sensors, consumables) and any exemptions.

catalysts.event: FDA follow-up on the January 2026 Libre warning letter (close-out or escalation)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The letter says Class III PMAs reasonably related to the violations will not be approved until the violations are addressed, and FDA has posted no close-out letter. A consent decree or second recall is a bear-case item (10%).
catalysts.watch: A close-out letter, the re-inspection outcome, any new Libre recall.

catalysts.why_it_moves: We deduct -$750M after tax. New batches or verdicts reprice the tail (the bear case carries Gill-like verdicts at 15%).
catalysts.watch: Settlement batches and the implied cost per infant vs our ~$76k, and new state-court trial settings.

risks.risk: The CGM slowdown runs longer or turns into share loss. Diabetes is guided to low-to-mid single digit for several quarters, and Medicare competitive bidding (bundled monthly rental) awards contracts in late summer/fall 2027 for pricing from 2028-01-01, inside the horizon NTM window.
risks.signpost: Q4 Diabetes Care comparable growth below ~3%, Dexcom gaining US share on 10-29 and after, a slipped Libre Duo launch, or bid single payment amounts well below today's rates.

risks.risk: The January FY2027 guide comes in below our ~$6.06. The street is still at $6.08 pre-print, and last year's initial guide was cut by April.
risks.signpost: An FY2027 adj. EPS guide well below $6.0, or organic growth guided below ~6% with no acceleration path. The supervisor ties a trade toward $78 (~12.1x NTM EPS, derived: 78 / 6.43) to impaired earnings power.

risks.risk: Litigation tails exceed our deductions: ~12,700 NEC infants at -$750M after tax, and Libre 3 recall claims (7 deaths, 860 serious injuries) at -$300M x 0.5.
risks.signpost: An NEC batch implying well above ~$76k per infant, a new nine-figure verdict, a Libre consent decree or second recall.

risks.risk: Spin dis-synergies or a defensive-multiple de-rating. The supervisor gives 55% odds of stranded costs at RemainCo, and a recession / higher-rates de-rating is ~-$1.9/share in the bear case.
risks.signpost: Form 10 terms with heavy stranded costs or little cash paid to Abbott, one-time charges well above ~$400M pre-tax, or peer NTM P/E median falling toward ABT's 16.5x.

trade.position: 16 sh held (~$1,639 at $102.45, 7.0% of the $23,529 book, derived: 16 x 102.45 = 1,639.20 / 23,529.49 = 6.97%; bought 2026-10-20 @ $102.80). The plan target is 34 sh: sizing.target_shares 34.45 is the 15% name cap, which binds because the tangency weight (0.39) is above it. (Sources 26, 27, 29.)
trade.entry: This follows the supervisor's two-tranche plan from the 2026-10-14 run: half before Q3 and half after the print once the H2 ramp is visible. The first tranche of 16 sh is done. The ramp showed up only in part: Q3 was +7.0% comparable, but the FY guide was cut to ~6.0%, so the add is not automatic. The second tranche (+18 sh on the plan, to 34) is staged after the Q3 print. The nightly re-mark on the 2026-10-21 post-print close will re-size it and Sharpe-test it, and we trade no earlier than 2026-10-22. Every level here is from the pre-print $102.45 close, and ABT traded ~$98 intraday after the print ($98.36, low $97.73). (Sources 1, 10, 26, 28, 30.)
trade.exit_or_add: We exit on a close below the $82.70 stop (15th percentile; ~$322 below cost on 16 sh, derived: (102.80 - 82.70) x 16 = $321.60) or a sustained trade below the $78 thesis break. We take profit at $133.60 (75th percentile; touch probability 0.434 vs 0.358 for the stop). The pre-print decider ladder will be redrawn tonight because its research is fixed in dollars. It holds 34 sh at $102.45 and 36 sh at $97.33 with no news check, and 38 sh at $92.20 and 42 sh at $81.96 only after a news check. It holds 16 sh with no add above ~$111.67 and has no trim level below $276. Separately, a January FY2027 guide at or above ~$6.0 supports building to the cap, and a guide well below it means re-running before adding. (Sources 24, 25, 28.)

what_changes_our_mind: Tonight's re-mark on the post-print close. If the re-run target falls below the price, or the add fails the Sharpe test, we skip the second tranche and stay at 16 sh. If it holds above the price, we add up to the re-sized amount from 2026-10-22.

The January 2027 guide. FY2027 adj. EPS at or above ~$6.0 with organic growth accelerating from ~6% confirms the build, and we build toward 34 sh. A guide well below $6.0, or diabetes still decelerating in Q4, breaks the earnings leg of the thesis, and we cut and re-run.

Litigation and Libre quality. An NEC settlement batch above ~2x our ~$76k per infant, or a Libre consent decree or second recall, means our deductions are too small and we cut. A CMS non-insulin type 2 coverage decision or a warning-letter close-out is upside not in the numbers, and we would add on weakness.
